options.text: Precise but biased, so it is inaccurate until the systematic error is corrected

items.stem: Which TWO practices reduce the risk of an overfit chemometric model? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Validating on an independent held-out data set
options.rationale: Correct: held-out validation reveals poor generalisation.

options.text: Limiting model complexity relative to the number of samples
options.rationale: Correct: fewer free parameters reduce overfitting.

options.text: Maximising the training-set fit at all costs
Using every available wavelength without selection

items.stem: Why report a measurement with its uncertainty rather than a single number?

options.text: It communicates the range within which the true value plausibly lies
options.rationale: Correct: uncertainty conveys confidence in the result.

options.text: Uncertainty makes the result look less reliable for no reason
options.rationale: Stating uncertainty is good practice, not a weakness.

options.text: A single number is always sufficient
options.rationale: Without uncertainty the result cannot be judged fit for purpose.
It is essential for real decisions on data.
